Resolves #19270

`CellEditingPickerProjection`'s date arms now reopen the picker from a closed state. A pick leaves the date picker open (`hidePickerOnSelect` is `false`) and the trigger toggles, so the arm's old second click closed the picker about 300 ms later. The scroll then started from a closing picker, which made "no picker floats over the vanished field" true whether or not projection worked. The arm now asserts the picker open after the pick, closes it, asserts it closed, and opens it again.

Micro-review eligible: test-only — one spec step, no product change.

Evidence: L2 (the e2e spec, local, including a CPU-throttled repeat) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-3). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Outside-CI probe at dev `a87a89e293`. The original reopen reads picker counts 1 → 1 (after 150 ms) → 1 (right after the click) → 0 (300 ms later). With the fix, a 400 ms hold after `open()` reads 1 in both date arms |
| AC-2 | Outside-CI: date arms 16/16 under `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 4, via `--repeat-each=8` (probe removed afterwards) |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the combo arms are untouched and pass (4/4 for the whole spec locally) |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive. Locally the original arm did not go red: 16/16 at 4x CPU, and 2/2 with a settle. Grace measured 9/16 and 6/6. The ticket body now carries both measurements and the vacuity finding.

## Test Evidence
Probes above, all removed before the commit. Whole spec 4/4 at the head.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] No `CellEditingPickerProjection` date-arm red in e2e-engine over the next ten dev runs.
